newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar breaks above $300 resistance.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar breaks above $300 resistance.

text.p: London's white sugar contract suddenly burst through the key $300 barrier in early Friday trading as commission house buying pushed spot March out of the week's tight range.
Two commission houses were cited as the principal instigators of the rally, later joined by a trade house which continued its recent buying programme at the higher levels.
The purchases were said to be mainly outright.
March jumped $3.90 in the early part of the session to hit an intraday high of $302.00, where it stood at 1245 GMT. May rose $3.10 to $300.00.
Volume amounted to a respectable 1,978 lots.

Traders said Indonesia's recent purchases of lesser-quality Thai white sugar was likely to be the physical background to the firmness, although steady buying has also been seen from Pakistan and Iran.
"The Indians may start coming out at these higher levels but it may take a time to filter through," said one.

With New York expected to open higher due to the strength in London, much interest should be fixed on whether the raws stage a rally and keep the spot white premium in line, especially as sellers are thought to be waiting in the wings at $70 and above.
Paris followed a similar pattern to London, with both nearby positions gaining ground in solid volume.
March was up $2.80 at $301.50 and May up $2.30 at $299.50. Matif volume amounted to 1,558 lots, mostly in March.
